newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Old Mutual assets jump to 198 bln rand.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Old Mutual assets jump to 198 bln rand.

text.p: South Africa's leading life assurer, Old Mutual, said on Monday that assets under management increased by 28 percent to 198.1 billion rand in the financial year to June 30, 1996.
Premium income climbed to 23.2 billion rand with individual and group business contributing 13.8 billion and 9.4 billion respectively.
Total group investment income rose 15.9 percent to 8.2 billion rand, while total income rose to 31.8 billion rand from 28.4 billion rand.
Chief operating officer Gerhard van Niekerk said benefits paid to clients increased 32.8 percent to 18.5 billion rand, which equated to 74 million rand each working day of the year.

"To provide for future payments to policyholders and beneficiaries, an additional 9.2 billion rand has been transferred to policyholders' funds which now stand at 166.7 billion rand -- 29.2 percent up on the previous year," van Niekerk said.
He said that in the past year, the South African life insurance industry had grown by 23 percent, with net premium income increasing from 48.3 billion rand to 59.5 billion rand.
"Of that increase, Old Mutual's share was 39.8 percent -- far ahead of any other life assurer," Van Niekerk said.
He said Old Mutual would continue to expand its leadership position in southern Africa while also establishing and growing profitable operations in selected global markets.
